description: This line plot, titled “Ablation Study on HateXplain Dataset,” illustrates the performance of five different model variants on three classification metrics: Precision, Recall, and F1-score, all measured as percentages. The x-axis, labeled “Model Variants,” is categorical and lists five conditions: “Full model (Ours),” “w/o Prompt,” “w/o Augmentation,” “w/o Attention,” and “w/o Prompt & Augmentation.” The y-axis, labeled “Metric (%),” is a linear scale ranging from 56 to 66, with major gridlines and tick labels at intervals of 2 percentage points (56, 58, 60, 62, 64, 66). The legend identifies three lines: Precision (purple line with circular markers), Recall (blue line with circular markers), and F1-score (brown line with circular markers). The “Full model (Ours)” achieves the highest scores across all three metrics: 65.49% for Precision, 65.56% for Recall, and 65.78% for F1-score. Removing the prompt (“w/o Prompt”) causes a significant drop in all metrics, with Recall falling to 59.64%, Precision to 61.06%, and F1-score to 60.16%. Removing augmentation (“w/o Augmentation”) results in a moderate decline, with Recall peaking at 63.75%, Precision at 62.22%, and F1-score at 62.63%. Removing attention (“w/o Attention”) leads to a further decrease, with Recall at 59.17%, Precision at 64.06%, and F1-score at 59.67%. The most degraded performance occurs when both prompt and augmentation are removed (“w/o Prompt & Augmentation”), yielding Recall of 56.82%, Precision of 65.44%, and F1-score of 57.74%. The plot visually demonstrates that the full model outperforms all ablated variants, and that removing key components, particularly the prompt, leads to substantial performance degradation.
